key_insight: A combined CEL simulation and ANN workflow can accurately predict temperature, force, and defect formation in friction stir welding of HDPE, enabling fast identification of weld-quality windows.
engineering_relevance: The study provides practical process guidance for improving thermoplastic weld quality by tuning rotational speed, travel speed, and bottom preheating to reduce defects and stabilize axial forces.
method: 3D Coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model of FSW under varied process settings
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental time-series data
Process-map generation to separate defect-free from defective welding conditions
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved strong predictive performance with R2 values of 0.91 to 0.99, and the CEL results matched experiments for temperatures, forces, and void formation.
watch_item: The models are validated on a limited parameter space, so performance may drop when extrapolated to new tool designs, material grades, or wider operating ranges.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
